metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in early January to assess progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Bolivia agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the possibility of holding the joint meeting on January 4th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike

Hey Kim, I was thinking... what do you think about holding the joint meeting on January 4th? It seems like a good time to assess our progress. 

Also, I’ve been curious... why do so many people criticize having the army rule? It’s not *exactly* seen as a bad thing everywhere.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
January 4th could work... but I think we should consider if everyone can make it. Maybe we should check with the other teams first. 

As for the army rule, in Bolivia, it's generally viewed negatively because of past experiences. People believe it can lead to oppression and limit freedoms. It’s important to keep that in mind when discussing governance.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, checking with the other teams sounds good. Let’s make sure we get everyone’s input before finalizing the date.

We all want what's best for our communities, right?
